thread:
sam: Heads-up — Acme POC is seeing streaming disconnects + partial SSE chunks from Android SDK behind their corp proxy. Repro steps below, logs attached.
liz: Which SDK version? Is the proxy doing HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 translation?
jordan: Also curious if it's a proxy MTU/chunk rewrite issue; those split SSE `data:` frames badly.
sam: SDK 1.4.2 (android). Customer uses an on-prem corp proxy that does TLS termination.
sam: Log snippet from the device (raw SSE):
```
:keepalive
data:{"id":"1","text":"Hello, wor"

data:{"id":"1","text":"ld"}
\n
```
sam: Notice the first event was split mid-json — client throws "Unterminated string" parse error.
liz: Can you paste the HTTP response headers? Any Transfer-Encoding or Content-Length weirdness?
sam: Headers we see proxied back:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked
x-proxy-id: corp-proxy-7
```
jordan: transfer-encoding: chunked + proxy rewriting is a smell. Proxy might be splitting chunks arbitrarily, breaking SSE chunk boundaries. Two quick checks: 1) try curl --no-buffer through the same proxy to see raw stream, 2) capture tcpdump on backend if possible.
sam: curl repro (from customer env):
```
curl -v -x http://corp-proxy:8080 "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=x" --no-buffer
```
Output shows multiple tiny chunk frames and truncated events.
mike: Short-term workaround: implement client-side buffering until you see a full SSE event (i.e., event ends with a double newline). Client should join partial `data:` lines and only parse once complete. Also increase reconnect backoff and tolerate duplicate event IDs.
infra-bot: Created POC ticket POC-5172 and linked logs: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/POC-5172
liz: Can you also grab the x-request-id from our side for one of the failing attempts? If you share the id we can correlate backend logs and proxy logs. Also try toggling `streaming_chunk_buffer_ms`=100 on our edge as a temporary mitigation.
sam: After enabling `streaming_chunk_buffer_ms=100` on the edge, customer reports much fewer parse errors but still occasional "Unexpected end of stream". Stack trace from Android client:
```
java.io.IOException: Unexpected end of stream
	at okhttp3.internal.http1.Http1ExchangeCodec.readResponseHeaders(Http1ExchangeCodec.java:189)
	at okhttp3.internal.http.CallServerInterceptor.intercept(CallServerInterceptor.java:88)
```
jordan: That okhttp trace suggests the underlying TCP/connection is being closed mid-chunk by the proxy. Longer-term fixes: 1) have server always terminate SSE events with `\n\n` and pad small events to avoid tiny chunk splits, 2) update Android SDK to buffer partial `data:` frames and reassemble before JSON parse, 3) add a small SSE `retry:` field so clients can re-establish faster.
jordan: I'll file a follow-up against runtime to ensure consistent event separators and add a note to SDK team. :thumbsup:
sam: Thanks — I'll pass this to Acme and propose a short troubleshooting call to capture tcpdump. Will update POC-5172 with results and schedule next steps.
